title.value: The Hidden Uniform Cluster Prior in Self-Supervised Learning
title.justification: The title is directly stated in the paper.
title.quote: T HE HIDDEN UNIFORM CLUSTER PRIOR IN SELF - SUPERVISED LEARNING

extractions.description: This paper explores the biases in self-supervised learning frameworks that lead to uniform clustering of data, a problem that can degrade performance in class-imbalanced settings. The authors propose an alternative approach, Prior Matching for Siamese Networks, that incorporates power-law distributed feature priors to improve representation learning on imbalanced datasets. Empirical validation shows that this method results in better semantic representations and improves performance on downstream tasks.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on theoretical advancements in machine learning and representation learning rather than direct applications to eco-responsible categories.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we show that many common self-supervised learning frameworks have a prior to capture features that enable uniform clustering of the data, and as such, require class-balanced datasets to learn class-discriminative features.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category is not applicable as the paper is not related to eco-responsible applications.
primary_sub_category.quote: Finally, based on this observation, we propose to move away from conventional uniformity priors and instead reformulate self-supervised criteria to prefer long-tailed feature priors that are more aligned with the distribution of semantic concepts in real-world datasets.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper deals with improving machine learning techniques for representation learning, especially in imbalanced datasets, which is a core area of machine learning optimization.
new_primary_category.quote: By reformulating self-supervised criteria to prefer power-law distributed features, one can improve quality of the learned representations on real-world class-imbalanced datasets.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on improving self-supervised learning techniques for datasets with imbalances, proposing new methods for better data representation.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We extend Masked Siamese Networks (MSN) to support the use of arbitrary features priors, and refer to this extension as Prior Matching for Siamese Networks (PMSN).
